body: @dsnopek I saw that the bug wasn't fixed in the latest Beta 6. Is there anything I can do to get PCVR working again? I'm currently beta testing my commissioned work and have to deliver it on September 1st. My contract specifies WebXR for Quest 2/3 and PCVR. I think I'll have problems there.

Sorry, I haven't had a chance to look into this yet - I usually develop on Linux, and any time an issue requires me to reboot into Windows, I tend to put it off. :-) I'll try to take a look soon!

As far as if you want to help: what I'll probably do when I dig into it, is add some `console.log()` statements around the JavaScript code that initializes WebXR to try to get an idea of where things are going wrong. If you were comfortable with building Godot, you could try to do that as well? The issue seems to happen very early, because one of the first things Godot's WebXR support does is attempt to make the WebGL context compatible with WebXR.

The most suspicious thing from the logs you posted is the first line:

```
WebGL: CONTEXT_LOST_WEBGL: loseContext: context lost
```

It could be that the WebGL context was lost sometime before it attempts to make it WebXR compatible? And, if so, attempting to narrow down what Godot was doing when that happened may help to point at the issue

I just did some testing using a very simple test project on Windows 11 with Godot 4.5-beta6 and Chrome 139.0.7258.139, using a Quest 3 streaming with either Quest Link or Steam Link, and it works fine for me.

I tried removing the polyfills and then I got a similar pop-up to the one in the description ("Unable to initialize WebXR: Unable to make WebGL context compatible with WebXR"), however, I didn't get the message in the console about the WebGL context being lost.

Are you sure that you're using _both_ polyfills? I don't think the basic WebXR one is required for Chrome, but the WebXR Layers one definitely is. You can add this code to the "Head Include" field in your export settings:

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/webxr-polyfill@latest/build/webxr-polyfill.min.js"></script>
<script>
var polyfill = new WebXRPolyfill();
</script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/webxr-layers-polyfill@latest/build/webxr-layers-polyfill.min.js"></script>
<script>
var layersPolyfill = new WebXRLayersPolyfill();
</script>
```

I also tried the Godot XR Tools demo from its git `master` branch (which includes both polyfills) and it entered WebXR just fine. I end up being stuck in the staging area for some reason, but I suspect that's some other unrelated bug, because I am able to successfully enter immersive mode in the headset.

This was all with Quest Link and Steam Link, though. I wasn't able to get streaming working with Virtual Desktop, although, I think I'm missing a step. I'm not sure how to make the browser see Virtual Desktop: I only get the "Your browser doesn't support immersive-vr. Sorry!" popup

@dsnopek This is getting complicated. I was able to conduct further tests with three friends. We all had the same behavior. We tested for several hours, always with the same results. I was able to gain the following new insights.

1. This probably has nothing to do with the actual bug (switching to VR mode). At most, it's a new bug. The XR-Tools demo project does start, but it gets stuck in the intro scene. It currently doesn't work in the PCVR browser at all, at least if the thread support setting is disabled. As soon as thread support is enabled, the app continues to run. As I said, this probably has nothing to do with the actual problem.

2. Now for the really important insight: As soon as I load another PCVR app in my browser (anything except a Godot VR app) and leave the browser tab open, then open a new tab with my Godot app (or refresh an already loaded Godot VR tab), everything works in Godot WebXR, and I switch to VR mode normally. Here's an example ThreeJS VR app that I'm running in the background: https://threejs.org/manual/examples/webxr-basic.html
The strange thing is, I don't even have to switch to VR mode with the other app; it's enough to just load the web page with the VR button.

Test scenario:
Open the following WebXR ThreeJS app: https://threejs.org/manual/examples/webxr-basic.html
Open the Godot WebXR app on itch.io: e.g.: https://malcolmnixon.itch.io/vertigo-maze. (It doesn't matter how old the Godot version is that the WebXR project was created with; the effect is always the same.)

And Malcolm's great app works.
If you close the browser and open Malcolm's app first, you can't get into VR mode, and a WebGL error occurs.

By the way, I've uploaded two Godot XR Tools demos to itch.io.
1. A version with thread support: https://rumariovr.itch.io/godot-xr-tools-demo-with-thread-support-option
2. A version without thread support: https://rumariovr.itch.io/godot-xr-tools-demo
@dsnopek Virtual Desktop. You have to set this option:

@RumarioVR Does the issue happen for you if you use Steam Link or Quest Link? I'm just trying to narrow down if this is specific to Virtual Desktop, or if there's something else I need to do in order to reproduce it with Steam Link or Quest Link.

I'll try the Virtual Desktop setting you suggested the next time I'm on Windows.

Well, I haven't had any good results with Steam Link so far. The WebXR apps (not just Godot apps) start, if at all, on the second attempt. There is no native support for Steam Link either. You either have to install a special browser in Steam or enable the OpenXR option in your desktop browser. There is also an OpenXR option in the Steam VR setup, but this isn't properly supported for WebXR. Unfortunately, Meta Remote Desktop doesn't support WebXR either. I don't use Meta Link or Meta Air Link because they still don't work on some gaming laptops (I use HP Omen laptops), at least not when using the latest drivers. Meta is simply hopeless. I tried to get the problem sorted out with them, and was able to speak to the developers directly and provide them with data, but after two weeks the developers were no longer working at Meta. I didn't feel like going through the whole support hierarchy again. It was also announced that Meta Link and PCVR would no longer be developed. Long story short, anything other than Virtual Desktop makes no sense in my opinion.

Hm, interesting. Both Quest Link and Steam Link worked for me with no additional configuration. I guess that's the challenge with targeting PC: things work a little differently on everyone's machines :-)

> Virtual Desktop. You have to set this option:

I tried that, but, unfortunately, it didn't help. The browser would just keep saying that VR was not supported.

However, that setting gave me the idea to try the other option ("SteamVR") and start SteamVR when using Virtual Desktop. Normally, when I use Virtual Desktop, I just launch things from the game launcher in the headset, and things just work, so it didn't occur to me to start SteamVR. Anyway, after I did that, then I was able to enter immersive mode with my Godot WebXR project!

However, with Virtual Desktop and "SteamVR", I did experience an issue: my controllers aren't tracking (not in any of my attempts with this configuration). That's something to look into! However, it's not the same as your issue :-/

Am I supposed to be running SteamVR together with the "VDXR" option? That seems odd to me, but when I do that, I still am able to enter immersive mode, however, there seems to be about ~20 seconds of blackness in the headset before I see what I expect from my project. It feels like it's taking a really long time to "start" or something? I don't really know how to verify if the "VDXR" option is doing anything, or if it's just using "SteamVR" anyway because I have SteamVR running.

So, I still haven't been able to reproduce the problem that this issue is about. If you have any additional advice on how I may do that, it would be appreciated!

I've now had well over 50 of my VRChat friends try to access the XR-Tools demo on itch.io. Unfortunately, it never works (just like all the other Godot WebXR apps on itch.io). I've described in detail above how to get it working. Neither ThreeJS nor vanilla WebXR loses the device contest. Unfortunately, I've noticed something else. Unlike WebXR on the Quest, MSAA doesn't work with PCVR. And what's even more worrying is that the performance is a disaster. It's clearly not using hardware acceleration, even though it's enabled in the Chrome browser. @dsnopek I can make all of next week available so we can try to solve this problem together.
